items.title: Scaffold the project
items.body: Create the folder layout, add a `dev` script, and confirm it boots.
items.plain: Create the folder layout, add a run script, and confirm the project starts.

items.title: How to run the dev loop
items.body:
1. `npm install`
2. `npm run dev`
3. Open http://localhost:3000

If the port is busy, set `PORT=3001`.
items.plain: The steps to run the project locally: install, start the dev server, and open it in your browser; change the port if it is busy.

items.title: Wire up the signup form
items.body: Capture email, validate it, store it. No auth yet — that is deferred (see decisions).
items.plain: Build the signup form that takes an email, checks it, and saves it. Accounts and login are left for later.

items.title: Which fields do you want on signup?
items.body: Right now the form only asks for email. Want a name field too, or keep it to one input for a lower barrier?

notes.author: founder
notes.body: Keep it to just email for launch. We can add name later if we need it.

notes.author: agent
notes.body: Got it — single email input it is. Marked this decision so we remember why.

items.plain: Right now signup only asks for an email. Do you want a name field too, or keep it to one box so it is easier to fill in?

items.title: Buy the production domain
items.body: Needs a human with the payment card to purchase the domain and point DNS. Parked until you have a minute.

items.title: The new tagline and why
items.body: Headline is now **"Track what you decided, not just what you did."** — it leads with the memory angle, which is the differentiator. Old one led with "roadmap", which every tool claims.
items.plain: The new headline leads with the memory angle, which is what sets the product apart, instead of the word every other tool uses.
